extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants (PIs/Co-PIs), administering organizations, and grant administrators preparing Spencer Foundation grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and applicant eligibility, submission, budgeting, and program-specific restrictions that apply to proposals submitted to The Spencer Foundation across its grant programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The information below applies to all Spencer grant programs, unless specifically noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher experience (PI/Co-PI degree requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators (PIs) and Co-PIs named on a proposal to The Spencer Foundation must have an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: Two programs (Research-Practice Partnership and Vision Grants) allow PIs/Co-PIs to have an earned doctorate, OR demonstrated professional experience appropriate to the program, OR a terminal degree in a professional field. Graduate students may be part of the research team but may not be named the PI or Co-PI on the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on holding multiple active Spencer research grants
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs are restricted from holding more than one active research grant from the Spencer Foundation at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction includes National Academy of Education (NAEd)/Spencer Dissertation and Postdoctoral fellowships, unless the Spencer grant is for a project that substantially differs from the NAEd/Spencer fellowship funded project. See policy on Dual Submissions for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI agreement and disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must acknowledge that they have read, understood, and agree to comply with the Spencer Foundation policy on the responsible and ethical use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy outlines responsible and ethical use of generative AI across Foundation operations, programs, and activities; applicants will be asked to acknowledge compliance during submission and can read the policy via the provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Spencer Foundation does not award grants directly to individuals. All proposals must be submitted by an administering organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administering organization must have a U.S. IRS non-profit determination (e.g., university, college, research organization, school district, 501(c)(3) non-profit, NGO).

rubrics_metrics.name: International organization eligibility and equivalency determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Spencer is open to receiving proposals from organizations outside of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the organization does not have a U.S. IRS non-profit determination, it will be expected to have an Equivalency Determination certificate. This is not required to submit a proposal, but if chosen for funding the Spencer Foundation will work with the organization to obtain certification through NGOSource. Grantee organizations are responsible for navigating local laws and policies to meet Spencer's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational sign-off on proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted proposals must be reviewed and signed by an authorized representative of the administering organization, accepting full responsibility for expenditure of the funds should the grant be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authorized sign-off is typically a grants and contracts or finance administrator. This requirement does not apply at the Intent to Apply stage for programs that use that stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on simultaneous multiple submissions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may not submit more than one application (including preproposals) to the Spencer Foundation at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies to the Small Grants, Large Grants, Racial Equity, and Research-Practice Partnership programs. If the PI or any Co-PI currently has an application under consideration in any of these programs, they must wait until a final decision has been made on the pending application before submitting a new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on receiving funding for the same work from multiple Spencer programs
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, PIs cannot receive funding from two Spencer research grant programs for the same work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision Grants exception to submission/holding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may apply for a Vision Grant even if they have another active Spencer research grant or another Spencer grant proposal in review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the projects proposed in a Vision Grant proposal and in another Spencer grant program proposal must be distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAEd/Spencer fellowship interaction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit applications to both the NAEd/Spencer fellowship program and a Spencer grant program with the same project idea, you must notify the Spencer administrative contact for the grant program to which you are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to timing of decision timelines: if you become a semifinalist for either program, you must choose to withdraw your proposal from either the fellowship or the Spencer grant competition. For both competitions, you must choose to withdraw from one. If you are a NAEd/Spencer Fellow or Research Development Awardee, you may be eligible to be a PI or Co-PI on a Spencer proposal only if the proposed project is significantly different from the fellowship project. NAEd/Spencer Postdoctoral Research Development Awardees are eligible to apply for and receive a Spencer grant award as PI or Co-PI for the same project recognized by the Research Development Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs — threshold and allowed rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Spencer Foundation does not allow indirect costs on grant awards of $75,000 or less. Research grant proposals with budgets of more than $75,000 may include indirect costs of 15% of the total direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most institutional infrastructure costs should not be included when calculating direct costs. Examples of non-allowable institutional infrastructure costs: office rent, grants and contracts office expenses, institutional and departmental administrative expenses, institutional and departmental information technology expenses, and accounting and legal services. The Foundation does not pay government-approved overhead rates on research grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs on non-research grants and administrative expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not pay indirect costs on non-research grants (such as fellowships or training grants), regardless of budget total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative expenses for non-research projects may be built into the direct costs, with the exception of those related to institutional infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost calculation when subcontractors are included
rubrics_metrics.description: When the total research grant proposal budget is more than $75,000 and includes a subcontract budget(s), the lead organization and subcontractor(s) can include up to 15% indirect costs on their portion of the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sum of the indirect cost charges should not exceed 15% of the total research grant proposal budget.
